name: Boomerang
about: Her first calf was born in 2006 and she has had four more calves since then. She is named for the boomerang-shaped scar on her tail.
photoCredit: M. Zani/Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life/New England Aquarium. Taken under NOAA permit ####
photoDescription: Boomerang swims at the surface in the Bay of Fundy.

name: Resolution
about: Born off the coast of Florida on New Year's Day, his was the first right whale birth ever observed by researchers.
photoCredit: P. Hamilton/Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life/New England Aquarium. Taken under SARA #####

name: Shackleton
about: Named for the intrepid Antarctic explorer after a week-long adventure in the Delaware River as a yearling.

name: Aphrodite
about: A mother and grandmother, Aphrodite is named after the goddess of love because her callosity pattern is sometimes heart-shaped.
photoCredit: H. Pettis/Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life/New England Aquarium. Taken under NOAA Permit XXXXXXX
photoDescription: Aphrodite flukes at sunset in the Bay of Fundy.

name: Calvin
about: Orphaned at only 8 months, this mother was named for the spunky character in the "Calving and Hobbes" comic strip.

name: Gemini
about: One of our oldest whales, Gemini has fathered at least four calves in the population. He's named for twin scars on his back.

name: Manta
about: Named for his upturned flukes, which resemble a swimming manta ray, Manta is an active participant in surface active groups.
